Pirates didn't always wear eye patches because they lost an eye.
On a ship, sailors were constantly running between the bright deck and the pitch black cargo hold below.
And your eyes need time to adjust to the dark. It can take up to twenty minutes.
In the middle of a battle, twenty minutes is forever.
So one popular theory says, pirates kept one eye covered all the time.
That eye stayed ready for the dark.
When they ran below deck, they just flipped the patch to the other eye, and could see right away.
Historians aren't sure pirates really did this. But when MythBusters tested it, it worked.
So that eye patch might not have been hiding an injury. It might have been night vision.
